=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/validate_changed_files_syntax.sh:lines 257-260 (per-file annotation) and lines 299-303 (summary annotation) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both annotations are emitted at `::error` level when the YAML checker is unavailable. The actual failure is a validator outage (no PyYAML in the image), not a YAML syntax error.
  WHY: A consumer viewing the Actions run summary / PR checks page sees one red `::error` annotation per edited YAML file plus a red summary annotation. The annotation level advertises a syntax failure, but the validator's exit code (`VALIDATOR_UNAVAILABLE_EXIT=3`) and the heal runner's reason (`reason=validator_unavailable`) both classify this as an outage. Operators triaging from the Actions UI will misinterpret the failure mode (the entire premise of the PR description is that a missing checker must not be reported as a syntax error — the script still does exactly that to the UI).
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:lines 107-110 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `grep -E '^::error' "${root}/results/validation.log"` matches any line beginning with the literal characters `::error`, including `::erroring`, `::error-foo`, etc. The validator's own annotation is `::error file=...::YAML checker unavailable` (a workflow command with `file=`), and `grep -E '^::error'` also matches `::erroring` if a future validator emits one. The intended match is the GitHub Actions workflow-command form `::error file=...` or `::error::message`.
  WHY: A future validator change that emits, e.g., `::error_blame=foo::…` would be printed through the HEAL_ISOLATED_EDITOR prefix and might leak a non-workflow-command line that the runner happens to treat as one (the test guards `::stop-commands::injected`, but a `::error_blame=` style line would survive). Tightening the regex to `^::error(file=|::)` keeps both valid forms and rejects the loose ones; the test's `assert "stop-commands" not in result.stderr` already continues to pass with that pattern.
- agents.md:lines 2099 and 2344 (the two `VALIDATE_CHANGED_FILES_SYNTAX` insertions) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new log prefix is inserted between `APPLY_ANALYSIS_DISPATCHED` and `APPLY_ANALYSIS_CANDIDATES` in both the contractual stable-log-prefix list and the `LOG_PREFIX.name=` registry, rather than placed with the other validator / heal prefixes (`HEAL_ISOLATED_EDITOR`, `HEAL_SCOPE_REFUSED`, `WORKFLOW_HEAL_EVIDENCE`, `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEADLINE`, `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_FIRST_ERROR`).
  WHY: Position does not change runtime behaviour — the prefix name is unique and consumers match on the literal `VALIDATE_CHANGED_FILES_SYNTAX` token — but the misalignment makes the registry harder to scan by domain and violates the implicit grouping convention in the surrounding entries. Moving the two insertions next to the heal-side prefixes keeps the registry organised without changing any contract.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
